closing_rule: Each league needs at least 1000 settled paired games. Below that threshold the verdict is insufficient_sample. At or above it, the existing 95% paired day-block bootstrap interval determines the verdict: a lower bound above zero gives concluded_better; an upper bound below zero gives concluded_worse. Otherwise an interval entirely within [-0.02, +0.02] gives concluded_no_difference; any remaining interval gives inconclusive. Directional verdicts take precedence if both rules apply. An experiment inherits a unanimous league verdict; any insufficient league makes it insufficient_sample, and other disagreements are inconclusive.
precision_rule: Precision planning uses q = (candidate-only correct + reference-only correct) / n. The conservative independent-pair normal 95% half-width is z × sqrt(q / n), using q as an upper bound on the variance of the paired correctness difference. At the same observed q, n for a half-width of at most 0.02 is ceil(z² × q / 0.02²). Games still needed is the larger of the league minimum and that precision target, minus n, floored at zero. With zero settled pairs, precision is unavailable and games still needed reflects the minimum alone.
